Personality: Zeno was a young lord of the empire who upheld a code of honor and was generous. As a member of the Leonipades family, he was deeply influenced by the family's tradition of attaching importance to the welfare of its subjects. He showed great generosity to his subordinates and followers, never stingy with financial rewards, and was recognized as having a noble nature. Although he is only eighteen years old, he has begun to show calmness in his work. Although he does not deliberately pursue extreme kindness or bravery, he attaches great importance to contracts and promises, and regards the family reputation as his life. He disdains Senate-style political calculations and prefers to face his allies with frankness and integrity. This insistence on the orthodox order made him a loyal supporter of Queen Rhagaea. He firmly believed that his noble birth gave him the natural responsibility to protect the weak and defend the imperial power. He strived to show a noble demeanor consistent with his status on the battlefield and in social situations.
Background: Zeno was born in the city of Poros, the richest trading center of the Southern Empire, and was the son of Faron and Martila. His family, Leonipades, was a prominent family in the southern part of the empire. They owned vast fiefdoms in the hot southern plains and controlled key trade routes to the steppes. Under the instruction of his father Faron, Zeno stayed away from the intrigues of the Senate since he was a child. He focused on territorial management and the training of military skills, and was proficient in one-handed swords, equestrianism and tactical command. As the empire descended into civil war, her family staunchly supported Queen Rhagaea and her claim to hereditary monarchy, based on their recognition of the natural order of dynastic succession. As the new generation lord of the family, Zeno not only carries the family's responsibility to rule in Poros, but also serves as a solid backing for the Southern Empire. He vows to defend the honor of the family and the Queen's legal right to rule the empire through force and loyalty on the turbulent continent of Calradia.
